risk_countries.name: Iran
risk_countries.note: Vows 'all available means' against the US blockade, offering to reopen Hormuz within two days if hostilities, the blockade and sanctions end.
risk_countries.details:
Iran is answering the blockade with fire on Gulf hosts and with terms. On 21 November the Guard said it hit US Patriot radars at Bahraini bases in what it called retaliation for US attacks, citing Hengam Island; Bahrain said an Iranian strike set fire to a civilian industrial site in Sitra, with no injuries (Al Jazeera). That followed a US strike on a launch site on Qeshm on 17 November and Iranian drones on Kuwait and Bahrain.

On 23 November the foreign ministry said Iran will use all available means against the blockade, calling it military aggression, and that Hormuz could reopen within two days if the US halts hostilities, lifts the blockade and waives sanctions (Al Jazeera). It summoned Qatar's envoy the same day over a Qatar-Germany statement, and its courts claimed $290 billion in damages from the US (France 24). The US Treasury sanctioned more of its exchange houses and companies on 23 November.

risk_countries.name: Israel
risk_countries.note: Likud-Yashar unity talks ended without a deal on 22 November; Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government.
risk_countries.details:
President Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government on 7 November. Talks between Netanyahu's Likud and Eisenkot's Yashar on a unity government ended without a deal on 22 November, split over who would lead and over Ben-Gvir. Eisenkot, whose camp holds 48 seats, 13 short of a majority, has until 6 December with a possible 14-day extension, and his party has floated a minority government relying on outside Arab-party support (Al Jazeera).

Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister with authority over military decisions, including on Iran. Israeli tanks crossed the Gaza ceasefire line on 18 November, and strikes continue in Gaza and southern Lebanon.

risk_countries.name: Lebanon
risk_countries.note: Aoun told Hezbollah on 21 November that weapons outside the state are finished and told Iran to stop interfering; Israeli strikes continue.
risk_countries.details:
President Aoun used his independence-eve speech on 21 November to call on Hezbollah to disarm, saying the era of weapons outside the state is over, to tell Iran to stop interfering in Lebanon's affairs and to demand Israel's withdrawal from all Lebanese territory (Times of Israel). Talks on disarmament have stalled over Hezbollah's refusal. Israel holds a self-declared zone about 10 km deep along the border and continues strikes, shelling and demolitions in the south.

The army arrested three people smuggling 264 kg of explosives from Syria on 22 November; a security source said they had no party affiliation (The New Arab). Earlier a military court charged 13 people over a 780 kg explosives truck that Hezbollah said was its own. OCHA said on 30 October that more than 300,000 people displaced since March remained so; the board holds no newer figure.

risk_countries.name: USA
risk_countries.note: Struck an Iranian launch site on Qeshm on 17 November after calling strikes unlikely, and joined Xi and Putin's nuclear-war declaration on 19 November.
risk_countries.details:
Eight days after Trump called new Iran strikes 'quite unlikely', US jets struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island on 17 November, which US officials said answered Iranian aggression; Iran then launched drones at Kuwait and Bahrain (BBC). The blockade continues, and on 23 November the Treasury sanctioned Iranian exchange houses and companies in the UAE, Turkey and Hong Kong in Iran's shadow banking network (OFAC). Iran says it will use all available means against the blockade.

On 19 November Trump, Xi and Putin met in Shenzhen and issued a joint declaration that nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought; it set no arms limits and did not mention Ukraine or Iran (BBC, The Guardian). The US mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, which agreed a large prisoner exchange.

risk_countries.name: China
risk_countries.note: Hosted Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November; their declaration said nuclear war cannot be won but omitted Ukraine and Iran.
risk_countries.details:
Xi hosted the first three-way meeting with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November, at APEC. Their joint declaration said nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought and pledged UN reform and more oil supply, but set no arms limits and did not mention the Ukraine or Iran wars; Xi called for nuclear weapons to be prohibited and destroyed over time (BBC, The Guardian).

On trade, China extended the measures suspended after September's Washington summit to 10 January 2027, including critical-mineral export waivers (Reuters). Its licence requirement for exports of drone parts used by Russia took effect on 18 November. Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive on 23 November while it examines whether foreign intelligence targeted him through an affair with a woman US authorities suspect of spying for China; Beijing denies it (Times of Israel).

risk_countries.name: Taiwan
risk_countries.note: Warned of increasingly sophisticated Chinese election interference before 28 November local elections; a candidate was indicted under the anti-infiltration law.
risk_countries.details:
Taiwan votes in local elections on 28 November under warnings of Chinese interference. On 23 November Mainland Affairs Council deputy head Shen Yu-chung said Beijing's methods, from financing candidates to cognitive warfare and underground betting, are growing more sophisticated with AI; he cited a Taiwan People's Party council candidate in Taoyuan indicted on 20 November on charges including Anti-Infiltration Act offences (Focus Taiwan).

Military pressure remains high: Taiwan's defence ministry reported 49 Chinese military sorties in the 24 hours to 3 November, the year's highest, while the Liaoning led a strike group in the western Pacific (SCMP). Taipei says coast-guard patrols off its east coast and near Pratas rehearse a blockade.

risk_countries.name: Russia
risk_countries.note: Its corvette Merkury capsized at Benghazi after a 22 November drone strike Kyiv claims; it warned Estonia of 'the brink of an open war'.
risk_countries.details:
Russia's war is spilling over its neighbours' borders and beyond Europe. On 20 November two Kh-101 cruise missiles and a jet drone crashed in south-eastern Poland during one of Russia's largest attacks on Ukraine; Tusk called it intentional (BBC). On 22 November Ukrainian naval drones sank the corvette Merkury at Benghazi in Libya, Kyiv says; Russia's ambassador said it would not go unanswered (The New Arab).

On 23 November the foreign ministry summoned Estonia's chargé d'affaires over its closure of road crossings from 1 December, accused Tallinn of letting Ukrainian drones use its airspace, warned of 'the brink of an open war' and reserved 'comprehensive political and diplomatic measures' (The Moscow Times). Denmark expelled Russia's defence attaché over an assassination plot on 20 November. In Shenzhen on 19 November Putin joined Trump and Xi in declaring that nuclear war cannot be won; German media report Russia may launch a nuclear-armed satellite, which the Kremlin dismisses.

risk_countries.name: Saudi Arabia
risk_countries.note: A Houthi strike damaged the sovereign wealth fund's Riyadh tower on 19 November; the coalition keeps bombing Houthi targets.
risk_countries.details: Saudi Arabia is fighting a renewed war with Yemen's Houthis alongside its role as a US partner in the Iran war. On 19 November a Houthi attack damaged the 80-storey Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's financial district; civil defence reported no injuries and called it a flagrant violation of international law. Earlier in November a strike damaged an Aramco tower in the same district. The Saudi-led coalition said it hit 60 Houthi targets on 17 November.

risk_countries.name: UAE
risk_countries.note: An ADNOC-managed tanker was hit near Hormuz on 17 November, and Somalia expelled the UAE ambassador on 19 November, alleging an 'open invasion'.
risk_countries.details:
The UAE sits on both of the board's main tracks. It hosted the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November, which ended with agreement on the war's largest prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on territory (The Guardian).

Its shipping is exposed in the Strait: on 17 November the LPG tanker Tara Gas, managed by ADNOC Logistics & Services, was hit by a projectile north of Khasab; one crew member is missing and 11 were injured, and Omani rescuers took off 24 crew (Reuters, via gCaptain).

On 19 November Somalia ordered the UAE ambassador out within 72 hours, recalled its own envoy and accused Abu Dhabi of an 'open invasion' of its sovereignty (Al Jazeera). Earlier, the UAE attorney general said the FlyDubai co-pilot who attacked his captain had planned a suicide attack on Ben Gurion airport and acted alone.

risk_countries.name: Qatar
risk_countries.note: Shuttles between Tehran and Washington, but Iran summoned its envoy on 23 November over a Qatar-Germany statement criticising Tehran.
risk_countries.details:
Qatar remains the main channel between Washington and Tehran, but the channel is strained. A Qatari delegation held about two hours of talks in Tehran on 20 November; Iran's deputy foreign minister said they were not yet formal negotiations, and Foreign Minister Araghchi said discussing Hormuz is pointless until Iran's demands are met (Al Jazeera). On 21 November Qatar and Germany issued a joint statement urging Iran to cooperate with the IAEA, stop arming the Houthis and keep the Strait open; Iran summoned Qatar's chargé d'affaires on 23 November (The New Arab).

Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister was due to meet Secretary of State Rubio in Washington on 23 November. Earlier reporting described a Qatari bridge plan of blockade relief and IAEA access first, then a Hormuz reopening.

risk_countries.name: Oman
risk_countries.note: Its rescuers took 24 crew off the burning tanker Tara Gas on 17-18 November; UKMTO reported a tanker hit near Khasab on 21 November.
risk_countries.details:
Oman's Musandam peninsula, on the southern side of the Strait, has become the main strike zone for shipping. Omani emergency authorities rescued 24 crew from the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas after it was hit by a projectile north of Khasab on 17 November, with one person missing (Reuters, via gCaptain). On 21 November UKMTO issued two reports of a tanker hit by unidentified projectiles near Khasab, possibly the same vessel, with no casualties; Iran said a tanker hit a mine east of the strait (Al Jazeera).

Oman has named no attacker. Earlier its navy rescued 25 crew from the tanker Riti, and limpet mines hit the Louise 1 off Khasab on 29 October. Its waters carry much of the traffic still moving through Hormuz.

risk_countries.name: North Korea
risk_countries.note: The IAEA said on 18 November a new Yongbyon enrichment extension was externally complete by late October, a 'cause for serious concern'.
risk_countries.details:
North Korea is expanding its capacity to make bomb fuel. IAEA Director General Grossi told the Board of Governors on 18 November that a new extension to the Yongbyon enrichment facility was externally complete by late October, calling the expansion a cause for serious concern (France 24).

On 4 November South Korea's military said the North fired several missiles from the Sondok area toward the Sea of Japan. Kim Yo Jong called the FBI's attribution of the $6.3 billion Binance theft a provocation and ruled out talks while US hostility continues. The launches followed a claimed cluster-warhead test in late October.

risk_countries.name: Pakistan
risk_countries.note: Hosted Iran's foreign minister at a 16 November regional meeting and pledged to pursue US-Iran diplomacy; still a Mecca pact partner of Saudi Arabia.
risk_countries.details:
Pakistan is stretched on three fronts and trying to be indispensable on all of them. At the Economic Cooperation Organization meeting in Islamabad on 16 November, attended by Iran's foreign minister Araghchi, Foreign Minister Dar said Pakistan will pursue US-Iran diplomacy with regional support, and that better ties with Afghanistan depend on Taliban action against terrorism; no Afghan diplomat attended (Associated Press).

On 5 October it joined Saudi Arabia and Turkey in activating their Mecca defence pact, agreeing to provide forces for Saudi Arabia's defence against the Houthis; Turkey's parliament ratified the pact on 5 November. On its western border, fighting with the Taliban has continued, and on 17 October it suspended trade with Iran at the Taftan and Gabd crossings, citing security and smuggling.

risk_countries.name: Vatican
risk_countries.note: Pope Leo XIV rejected Trump's claim that the Holy See supports Iran's nuclear program; he met Secretary Rubio at the Vatican on May 7.
risk_countries.details:
The Vatican's posture is to distance the Holy See from the Trump administration's framing while keeping its diplomatic-venue offer open. Pope Leo XIV's remarks at Castel Gandolfo on May 5 directly rejected Trump's claim that he supports Iran's nuclear program.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met the Pope at the Vatican on May 7. The Holy See's stated framing — 'need to promote peace' — anchors both the meeting and the broader diplomatic offer.

The Vatican's neutral-mediator posture is reputational and procedural; there is no kinetic exposure. Watch-points: any formal Holy See offer to host ceasefire talks; any subsequent papal statement on Iran's enrichment program or the Lebanon framework.

risk_countries.name: Turkey
risk_countries.note: Parliament ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; troop deployments need a separate vote.
risk_countries.details:
Turkey's parliament approved the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement on 5 November by 279 votes to 119 (Iran International; The New Arab, citing Anadolu). The pact, signed in August, covers intelligence sharing, military coordination, joint deterrence and defence industry, and treats an attack on one member as an attack on all three. It does not authorise sending Turkish troops, which needs a separate vote, and Ankara says its forces will not take part in offensive operations against the Houthis.

A NATO member is now bound to defend Saudi Arabia, which is under Houthi missile fire. Turkey also began 'Sea of Friendship' naval drills with Egypt on 4 November.

risk_countries.name: India
risk_countries.note: Ordered tighter protection for Indian seafarers on 19 November, tracking nine India-linked vessels west of Hormuz after 15 deaths since March.
risk_countries.details:
India is shifting from appeals to protection for its seafarers. On 19 November Shipping Minister Sonowal directed the Directorate General of Shipping to tighten monitoring and advisories; the ministry is tracking nine India-flagged or Indian-interest vessels west of Hormuz and says 86 India-linked transits have been completed (BusinessToday).

An Indian crewman died when the dhow Al-Jusufi was hit near Limah in Omani waters on 3 November; India says 15 Indian seafarers have been killed near Hormuz since March. New Delhi has called for de-escalation and earlier warned that US tariffs on buyers of Russian oil would hurt ties.

risk_countries.name: Egypt
risk_countries.note: Its foreign minister said on 10 November Egyptian forces are already in Saudi Arabia at Riyadh's request, for air defence and site protection.
risk_countries.details:
Egypt is already part of Saudi Arabia's defence. In a France 24 interview on 10 November, Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Egyptian forces have been in Saudi Arabia for months at Riyadh's request, after attacks on the kingdom during the escalation with Iran; he described the mission as defensive, including air defence and protection of sensitive sites such as the holy places (Euronews). The deployment predates parliament's 26 October authorisation; some lawmakers told AFP they had received no details. Sisi says Egypt will not attack Yemen.

On 4 October Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan's army leader and Somalia's president declared at El Alamein that Red Sea governance belongs to littoral states, as Ethiopia presses for sea access.

risk_countries.name: Ethiopia
risk_countries.note: Ethiopia and Eritrea have massed forces along their border, conflict monitors say; clashes are reported but unconfirmed.
risk_countries.details: Fighting between Ethiopia's federal government and Tigrayan rebels broke out in September, and Ethiopia says Eritrean forces crossed into Tigray in early October. On 18 November ACLED and the International Crisis Group told Reuters that the two armies had massed within striking distance along the border; Reuters could not confirm reported skirmishes, and Eritrea's information minister dismissed 'propaganda'. Ethiopia did not comment.

risk_countries.name: United Kingdom
risk_countries.note: Joined the EU on 20 November in demanding Iran end hybrid attacks in Europe, and signed a pledge against Hormuz transit tolls.
risk_countries.details:
Britain is the main European stage for both of the board's adversary arcs. At the EU-UK summit on 20 November, leaders told Iran to stop its hybrid attacks on European soil, signed a 'No Tolls/No Fees' pledge on navigation through Hormuz and condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and shipping (Iran International). MI5 has reported more than 50 Iran-linked arrests in a year.

On 10 November the US Justice Department charged Iran-backed operatives over a plot at RAF Fairford, and the US moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall over an Iran-linked threat. The same day police arrested a US Army member near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia; no charge has been announced. Prime Minister Andy Burnham also agreed a wider EU deal on food checks, emissions trading and a youth scheme (BBC).

risk_countries.name: Iraq
risk_countries.note: Government forces entered Kataib Hezbollah's Jurf al-Sakhar base on 20 November; the group is to withdraw within a month.
risk_countries.details: Baghdad ordered its forces into Jurf al-Sakhar, Kataib Hezbollah's stronghold 60 km south-west of the capital, after an inquiry linked the group to oil smuggling through illicit refineries; nine senior officials were dismissed. A compromise reached on 19 November brought a joint force of army, federal police, energy police and Popular Mobilisation units into the town on 20 November, with the group expected to leave within a month. Prime Minister al-Zaidi told troops they were not waging war but that keeping weapons under state control was final. US and Gulf pressure was a driver. Earlier in November a drone hit the Khor Mor gas field, cutting power across much of Kurdistan.

risk_countries.name: Kuwait
risk_countries.note: Repelled an Iranian drone attack on Ali Al Salem air base on 18 November, its first in two months, and condemned it.
risk_countries.details:
Kuwait hosts US forces at Ali Al Salem air base and, since November, the advanced headquarters of the Gulf states' unified military command.

On the night of 17-18 November, after US jets struck Qeshm, Iran's army said its drones targeted US Patriot systems and launch platforms at Ali Al Salem. Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged the drones and reported no casualties or damage, and the foreign ministry said the attack flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty and was a grave breach of international law. It was the first Iranian attack on Kuwait in more than two months.

Kuwait's posture through the war has been to host the forces Iran targets while avoiding a public role in the fighting. A strike that causes casualties on Kuwaiti soil would test that directly.

risk_countries.name: Jordan
risk_countries.note: A court sentenced three men to death on 15 November for the Karak church attack, which killed nine; ISIS claimed it.
risk_countries.details:
Jordan's most serious attack this autumn came from inside. Gunmen opened fire at a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate on 23 October, killing nine, Al Jazeera reported; ISIS claimed it. Three wounded suspects were arrested on 26 October after a firefight, were charged with terrorism on 3 November and were sentenced to death by hanging by the State Security Court on 15 November (Al Jazeera).

On 26-27 October Jordan's air force struck what it called terrorist hideouts in southern Syria, saying it killed more than 20 fighters; Damascus condemned an 'unacceptable violation', the worst Amman-Damascus row since Assad's fall. Jordan also remains exposed to the Iran war: Iranian missiles were fired at the Al Azraq base in September, and it published interception counts without announcing measures against Iran.

risk_countries.name: Bahrain
risk_countries.note: An Iranian attack set fire to a civilian industrial site on 21 November, with no injuries; air defences intercepted several other attacks.
risk_countries.details: Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet and has been attacked repeatedly since the war began in February. After a lull of several weeks, Iranian drones and missiles have targeted it again since 13 November. On 21 November its air defences intercepted several attacks, but the Interior Ministry said one caused a fire at a civilian industrial facility, which it did not name, with material damage and no injuries. Iran's Guard said it targeted US Patriot radars at two bases. The Gulf Cooperation Council and Jordan condemned the attack.

risk_countries.name: Libya
risk_countries.note: A Russian corvette was sunk at Benghazi on 22 November; Ukraine claims the drone strike, and Libya's east seeks a UN probe.
risk_countries.details:
Libya has become a theatre of the Russia-Ukraine war. On 22 November the Russian navy corvette Merkury was struck at the Benghazi naval base in the east, held by Khalifa Haftar's forces; satellite imagery showed it capsized with only its bow above water. On 23 November Zelensky said Ukraine used seven naval drones, also hit the cargo ship Angara, which he said carried weapons, and destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter (Al Jazeera). Libyan officials told AP the drones were launched from western Libya.

The eastern administration condemned a violation of sovereignty and asked for a UN-led investigation; the UN mission called for an independent inquiry, and the Tripoli government rejected the use of Libyan waters for outside conflicts. Russia's ambassador said the attacks would not go unanswered (The New Arab). Ukraine's claim has no independent confirmation beyond the imagery.

In September the Tripoli government said it had dismantled a cell behind drone attacks on oil sites, without naming a backer.

risk_countries.name: Japan
risk_countries.note: Scrambled jets and protested after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace near Okinoshima on 17 November.
risk_countries.details:
Putin placed the Russian operations of Japan Tobacco International under state control on 5 November (Euronews; The Moscow Times); Tokyo demanded the return of four businesses. It follows a decree in October seizing several European firms' Russian assets.

Japan's role in the region otherwise centres on Okinawa basing, a debate on a large defence-spending increase, and coordination with the US ahead of APEC.

risk_countries.name: Romania
risk_countries.note: Investigating drone strikes on three ships off its coast on 13-14 November, one inside its territorial waters.
risk_countries.details:
Romania's coast is now where the Black Sea war kills sailors. On 23 October the Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv sank after a drone strike about 13 nautical miles off Constanta, just outside Romanian territorial waters; one sailor died, nine were rescued and three are missing. President Nicusor Dan said it was 'part of Russia's escalation process in its war in Ukraine'. Reuters counts at least seven cargo ships hit off Romania and Bulgaria in two weeks.

Romanian F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran drones over Romanian waters near Sulina on 17 October. NATO's council, meeting at Bucharest's request on 20 October, agreed to send more patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the Black Sea but no new command. Romania has proposed a rotating NATO Black Sea command it would host from 2028.

risk_countries.name: South Korea
risk_countries.note: Issued its first preliminary air alert over Russian aircraft on 24 November as about five warplanes neared Ulleung Island; Russia's attaché was summoned.
risk_countries.details:
On 24 November about five Russian warplanes entered South Korea's air defence zone over the East Sea and approached Ulleung Island, closer than a March 2025 flight; the Joint Chiefs issued a preliminary alert for the island, the first over Russian aircraft, and fighters scrambled, though no airspace violation occurred. The defence ministry summoned Russia's military attaché and called repeated entries unacceptable (Yonhap). An interior-ministry text wrongly said airspace had been breached.

President Lee named Lim Woong-soon foreign minister and Kang Kum-sil intelligence chief on 23 November. On the Iran war, the Cabinet approved on 10 November extending the Cheonghae unit's area to waters south of Oman, pending a National Assembly vote (Korea JoongAng Daily).

risk_countries.name: Germany
risk_countries.note: Joined Qatar on 21 November in urging Iran to stop arming the Houthis and keep Hormuz open; Tehran protested to Qatar.
risk_countries.details:
Germany has moved into the Iran file. A Germany-Qatar joint statement issued on 21 November, after the emir's visit, urged Iran to resume full cooperation with the IAEA, stop arming the Houthis, end ballistic-missile threats and attacks on shipping, and rejected any closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran summoned Qatar's chargé d'affaires on 23 November and called the statement baseless (The New Arab).

At home, counter-intelligence cases reached the top of the system: on 6 October prosecutors arrested August Hanning, a former BND chief, on suspicion of espionage for an unnamed foreign service, and in October the authorities raised the Russian sabotage threat level to 'significant'. Germany is one of five European states named to represent Europe at future Ukraine talks, and joins Lithuania, Poland and Bulgaria in a planned joint investigation into Starlink-site arson (LRT).

risk_countries.name: Canada
risk_countries.note: Sanctioned 38 entities and 24 people tied to Russia's missile industry, cyber actors and crypto enablers.
risk_countries.details:
Foreign minister Anita Anand announced new Russia sanctions on 9 November at the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris, adding 38 entities and 24 individuals linked to Russia's ballistic-missile industry, Russian cyber actors and financial enablers including crypto exchanges.

In September the EU invited Canada to become its first associate member, offering an alliance covering technology, defence industry, energy and critical minerals as Ottawa seeks less dependence on US trade. Canada's Treasury-sanctioned money-exchange firms that moved Iranian funds were named by the US on 6 November.

risk_countries.name: Syria
risk_countries.note: Weighs sending troops to defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis, the NYT reports; the US weighs a first training mission with its army.
risk_countries.details:
Syria is moving toward a military role in the Gulf war. On 10 November the New York Times reported, citing three officials, that Damascus is weighing sending thousands of troops to Saudi Arabia and Yemen against the Houthis, possibly under the Mecca defence pact; reconnaissance teams have visited and no decision has been made. Foreign Minister al-Shaibani had confirmed talks on joining the pact.

On 23 November Reuters reported the US is weighing a multinational demining and ordnance-disposal training mission for Syrian soldiers, the first US mission with Syria's military since Assad's fall; it could start in March (via Times of Israel). Syria said on 3 November it arrested a Hezbollah-linked cell planning to attack the Homs refinery. Relations with Jordan soured after Jordanian air strikes in southern Syria on 26-27 October.

risk_countries.name: Chad
risk_countries.note: Accused Sudan of an air strike near their shared border that killed twelve at a fuel market; Sudan has not responded.
risk_countries.details:
Chad borders Sudan's Darfur region and has absorbed large numbers of people displaced by that war. On 28 August its government accused Sudan of carrying out an air strike near the shared border, killing twelve people at a fuel market. Sudan has not responded, and no independent verification of responsibility has been published.

The allegation matters because this board has carried Sudan as an internal war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces. A cross-border strike between two states is a different object, and if substantiated it would widen the conflict rather than deepen it. Chad has previously been named in reporting as a transit route for supplies reaching the Rapid Support Forces, which both governments dispute.

The entry opens at a low risk level because the claim rests on one government's statement carried by a single outlet, with no attribution established and no second state confirming it.

risk_countries.name: Venezuela
risk_countries.note: Resumed military cooperation with the US during Defence Secretary Hegseth's unannounced visit to Caracas on 18 November.
risk_countries.details:
Venezuela has been governed since January by interim leader Delcy Rodríguez, Nicolás Maduro's former vice-president, with Washington's backing after US special forces captured Maduro and took him to New York for trial.

On 18 November US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth made an unannounced stop in Caracas, the highest-level US visit since Maduro's ouster, and announced renewed US-Venezuelan military cooperation against drug traffickers. Rodríguez hailed a 'resumption of the technical-military relationship.' Opposition leader María Corina Machado has returned from exile, but hundreds of political prisoners remain held and no election date has been set.

The US interest is oil and a Caribbean security footprint; the risk is that the arrangement entrenches the old state apparatus.

risk_countries.name: Ukraine
risk_countries.note: Says its naval drones sank the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi, Libya, on 22 November; Russia's envoy there says it will not go unanswered.
risk_countries.details:
Ukraine's strike war has reached the Mediterranean. Zelensky said on 23 November that Ukrainian forces used seven naval drones to sink the Russian corvette Merkury at Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya on 22 November, hit the cargo ship Angara and destroyed a Ka-27 helicopter; satellite imagery showed the corvette capsized (Al Jazeera, CNBC). The SBU said the drones were launched from a mother ship. A day earlier a drone set the Russian military-linked ship Sparta II ablaze in the Gulf of Finland; Kyiv has not claimed it.

On 20 November Russia launched one of its largest attacks of the war, during which two Kh-101 missiles and a drone crashed in Poland. Defence minister Umerov led Ukraine's team at the Abu Dhabi talks on 10-11 November, which agreed the war's largest prisoner exchange; no exchange had been reported by 23 November. Europe has named five governments to represent it at future talks.

risk_countries.name: France
risk_countries.note: Presented evidence on the Guard's supermarket cyberattacks to EU ministers on 16 November and expects sanctions at the 14 December Council.
risk_countries.details:
France made Europe's first government attribution of a large Iranian cyber-sabotage campaign: Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the Revolutionary Guard was behind attacks in October that raised fridge temperatures at hundreds of French supermarkets, and the Paris prosecutor requested arrest warrants for two officials. On 16 November Barrot presented the evidence to EU foreign ministers, said a very large majority backed a response and said he hopes sanctions will be adopted at the 14 December Council; he also announced a 4 December Paris conference on Russia's shadow fleet (French foreign ministry statement).

On Ukraine, France is one of five European governments named to represent Europe at future talks. It held a first joint forward-deterrence exercise with Sweden on 16-18 November and has pledged forces and air defences to protect Saudi Arabia's Yanbu port.

risk_countries.name: Hungary
risk_countries.note: Suspended rail services to Ukraine after a Russian drone hit Mukachevo on 17 November; Magyar plans to visit ethnic Hungarians in Zakarpattia.
risk_countries.details:
Under Péter Magyar, prime minister since May, Hungary has moved from the EU's most Russia-friendly government to one taking measures against Moscow: it designated Russia a threat in August and expelled ten Russian diplomatic staff on 8 September.

Relations with Kyiv are improving but unfinished. On 20 October Hungary blocked, without explanation, a procedural step toward opening the last two EU negotiating clusters for Ukraine and Moldova; diplomats expected the block to be temporary. After a Russian drone struck Mukachevo, near the Hungarian border, on 17 November, Hungary suspended all rail services to Ukraine. Magyar told parliament he will visit Zakarpattia soon to support its ethnic Hungarian community, and a Ukrainian official said Zelensky may meet him there (Kyiv Independent). Magyar still presses Kyiv on Hungarian-language schooling.

risk_countries.name: Poland
risk_countries.note: Russian cruise missiles fell on its soil on 20 November and a drone entered its airspace on 23 November; NATO agreed to give it an AWACS.
risk_countries.details:
On 20 November, during one of Russia's largest attacks on Ukraine, Russian cruise missiles fell at Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik nad Sanem and Molodycz in south-eastern Poland; first described as two missiles and a jet-powered drone, all three objects were later confirmed as Kh-101s, Kyiv Post reports. No one was hurt. Polish leaders called the timing, during an allied exercise at Nowa Deba, deliberate.

Late on 23 November a Russian drone entered airspace over the Lublin region, triggering an hour-long air alert; Deputy Defence Minister Zalewski called it deliberate (Kyiv Independent). He said NATO's council agreed on 23 November to give Poland an AWACS early-warning aircraft and deferred its other requests to next week's foreign ministers' meeting (Kyiv Post).

Earlier in November prosecutors charged a man over a Russian-directed train bombing.

risk_countries.name: Lithuania
risk_countries.note: Joined a planned four-country probe into Starlink arson, and rejected Russian claims that a Kaliningrad alert on 21 November was a Lithuanian attack.
risk_countries.details:
Lithuania is a front-line target of Russian hybrid pressure. Lithuania, Poland, Germany and Bulgaria plan a joint investigation team into arson attacks on Starlink sites, including a foiled attempt in Vilnius on 18 October; prosecutors are due to meet in early December (LRT).

On 21 November Kaliningrad's governor declared an air-raid alert over a 'suspicious object from the Lithuanian side', and Russian outlets then described an attack from Lithuania; the foreign ministry rejected the claim early on 22 November, and LRT, citing a monitoring firm, traced the narrative to a few social-media accounts. Lithuania has also handed Washington proposals for a permanent US military base, modelled on Germany's brigade there; no US answer has been reported.

risk_countries.name: Estonia
risk_countries.note: Named Russia's GRU for an arson attempt at drone maker Threod and plans to shut three road crossings with Russia on 1 December.
risk_countries.details:
Estonia is a NATO and EU member on Russia's border.

On 14 November an arson attempt at drone manufacturer Threod Systems was thwarted and eight Latvian residents were detained; Estonia's security service said Russia's military intelligence, the GRU, ordered it and that about ten defence firms were being targeted. The foreign minister said the Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa road crossings would close from 1 December, pending a cabinet decision. Moscow called the accusation baseless and the Kremlin said Estonia was 'building a wall.'

The question for this entry is the Russian response once the crossings close, and whether Latvia and Lithuania follow.

chess_players.name: United States
chess_players.goal: Reopen the Strait on American terms while the economic campaign does the rest of the work.
chess_players.move: Struck Iran's Qeshm on 17 November and widened sanctions on 23 November while holding the blockade; joined the Shenzhen nuclear-war declaration with Xi and Putin.
chess_players.details: Washington is running pressure on two tracks. On Iran it struck a missile launch site on Qeshm on 17 November (BBC), keeps the naval blockade, extended to ship-to-ship transfers, and on 23 November sanctioned Iranian exchange houses and companies (OFAC). On the great powers, Trump met Xi and Putin in Shenzhen on 19 November and signed a declaration that nuclear war must never be fought, with no arms limits (BBC, The Guardian). Envoys Witkoff and Kushner mediated the Abu Dhabi talks that agreed a Russia-Ukraine prisoner exchange.

chess_players.name: China
chess_players.goal: Keep buying Iranian oil and refuse the enforcement architecture, while raising maritime pressure on Taiwan without committing to a campaign.
chess_players.move: Hosted the first Trump-Putin-Xi summit in Shenzhen and its joint declaration, while licensing exports of drone engines Russia uses.
chess_players.details: Beijing used APEC in Shenzhen to stage the first three-way meeting of the US, Chinese and Russian leaders on 19 November. The joint declaration said nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, called for UN reform and more oil supply, and did not mention Ukraine or Iran. Xi pressed Trump on Taiwan and repeated China's call for nuclear weapons to be prohibited over time. From 18 November China requires export licences for drone components including jet engines used in Russia's Geran drones; Ukraine welcomed the step but says many parts remain uncontrolled.

chess_players.name: Taiwan
chess_players.goal: Hold operational readiness through Balikatan 2026 and post-summit PLA posture window; deepen alignment with Japan and the Philippines
chess_players.move: Warning of Chinese election interference before 28 November local elections; a council candidate was indicted under the anti-infiltration law on 20 November.
chess_players.details:
Taipei is defending its elections as much as its airspace. The Mainland Affairs Council warned on 23 November that Chinese interference is growing more sophisticated with AI, citing the 20 November indictment of a Taoyuan council candidate on anti-infiltration charges (Focus Taiwan). Earlier in November it logged 49 Chinese military sorties in a day as the Liaoning group drilled offshore (SCMP).

A $14 billion US arms package awaits Trump's approval, and Taiwan is trimming draft exemptions.

chess_players.name: Israel
chess_players.goal: Establish a permanent security posture in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza before any framework acquires enforcement, and absorb American objection without paying for it.
chess_players.move: Netanyahu stays caretaker with authority over Iran decisions after unity talks with Eisenkot collapsed on 22 November; Eisenkot's mandate runs to 6 December.
chess_players.details: Herzog gave Eisenkot the mandate on 7 November. Likud-Yashar unity talks ended without a deal on 22 November; Eisenkot has until 6 December, extendable by 14 days, and may try a minority government (Al Jazeera). Netanyahu stays caretaker with authority over military operations, including on Iran. Herzog and Trump want the next government to advance the US Gaza plan.

chess_players.name: Iran
chess_players.goal: Convert control of the Strait into sanctions relief and compensation, with Washington moving first.
chess_players.move: Struck Bahrain again and hit tankers near Khasab while receiving Qatari mediators; demands the US accept its conditions.
chess_players.details: Since the US struck Qeshm on 17 November, Iran has fired drones and missiles at Kuwait and repeatedly at Bahrain, where a 21 November attack set fire to a civilian industrial site. Its navy enforces what it calls coordinated passage through the strait; UKMTO logged three tanker-attack reports near Khasab on 20-21 November. The Guard claims it shot down two US drones. Tehran calls the US blockade an act of war and says it will act to break it, while a Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on 20 November that Iran says are not yet formal negotiations; it insists its enriched uranium stays in the country.

chess_players.name: Russia
chess_players.goal: Absorb strikes on export infrastructure without acknowledging damage, while keeping the war's economic pressure pointed at Ukraine through winter.
chess_players.move: Signed the Shenzhen joint declaration, then launched a mass strike on Ukraine in which cruise missiles crashed in Poland.
chess_players.details: Putin met Trump and then joined Xi and Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November for a declaration on nuclear war that left out Ukraine. He vowed a painful response to Ukraine's Crimean Bridge strikes; the 20 November attack was one of the war's largest, and two Kh-101 missiles and a drone crashed in Poland, which calls it intentional. Strikes damaged the Dutch and Austrian embassies in Kyiv. Denmark says Russian intelligence initiated a plot to kill a Ukrainian-American near Copenhagen, and expelled Russia's attaché; Moscow denies it. Estonia will close its road border from 1 December.

chess_players.name: Ukraine
chess_players.goal: Convert deep strikes from claimed damage into measurable losses of Russian export revenue and launch capacity.
chess_players.move: Says it took its naval-drone campaign to Libya, sinking a Russian corvette at Benghazi on 22 November, while the prisoner exchange agreed in Abu Dhabi is still pending.
chess_players.details: Kyiv is stretching Russia's defences across seas. It says naval drones sank the corvette Merkury at Benghazi on 22 November and hit the cargo ship Angara (Al Jazeera, CNBC), after its earlier strikes on Russian shipping in the Black Sea and the Gulf of Finland. Talks track: Umerov led the Abu Dhabi delegation on 10-11 November, which agreed a large prisoner exchange still pending on 23 November; US officials have discussed NATO-like guarantees. Russia keeps striking its energy system.

chess_players.name: Pakistan
chess_players.goal: Keep channels to both Washington and Tehran while making the Mecca pact a credible deterrent for Saudi Arabia.
chess_players.move: Pledged on 16 November to pursue US-Iran diplomacy, hosting Iran's foreign minister in Islamabad, while backing Saudi Arabia under the Mecca pact.
chess_players.details: Islamabad's play is to be indispensable to Riyadh and Washington at once: a Mecca-pact partner, a US-Iran mediator and a counter-terrorism front-line state. At the 16 November ECO meeting in Islamabad, with Araghchi present, Foreign Minister Dar said Pakistan will pursue US-Iran diplomacy with regional support (Associated Press). The Taliban border and the October halt to Iran trade show the cost.

chess_players.name: Vatican
chess_players.goal: Distance the Holy See from Trump's framing while keeping diplomatic-venue offer open
chess_players.move: Pope Leo XIV at Castel Gandolfo May 5 rejected Trump's claim he supports Iran's nuclear program; met Rubio May 7 — Vatican cites 'need to promote peace.'

chess_players.name: Saudi Arabia
chess_players.goal: Impose costs on Iran's proxy network without owning the escalation rhetorically or opening a second front in Yemen.
chess_players.move: Absorbing Houthi strikes, including damage to Riyadh's PIF tower on 19 November, as the Houthis claim a coalition strike killed 17 in Hodeidah.
chess_players.details:
Saudi Arabia is absorbing a sustained Houthi campaign on its territory. A Houthi attack damaged the 80-storey Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh's financial district on 19 November, with no one injured, after earlier hits on an Aramco tower in Riyadh and a pipeline in the Medina region. The coalition said it intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at the western Red Sea coast on 22 November.

Its forces are hitting back in Yemen: the coalition struck 60 Houthi targets on 17 November, and the Houthis said a coalition strike on telecoms facilities in Hodeidah killed 17 workers on 23 November, which Saudi Arabia did not address (The New Arab). Turkey ratified the Mecca defence pact on 5 November, and Syria is weighing sending troops.

chess_players.name: UAE
chess_players.goal: Keep the Strait open and stay out of the war, while holding the US relationship without joining an American campaign against Iran.
chess_players.move: Hosted Russia-Ukraine talks that agreed a large prisoner swap, while an ADNOC-managed tanker was hit near Hormuz and Somalia expelled its ambassador.
chess_players.details:
Abu Dhabi's strategy through this war has been to absorb rather than escalate and to stay useful to Washington. It hosted the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks on 10-11 November, which agreed the war's largest prisoner exchange (The Guardian).

The costs are rising. The ADNOC-managed LPG tanker Tara Gas was hit north of Khasab on 17 November, leaving one crew member missing and 11 injured (Reuters, via gCaptain), and on 19 November Somalia expelled the UAE ambassador, accusing it of an 'open invasion' (Al Jazeera). It is also redesigning a planned AI data-centre campus into a dispersed network because of the Iranian threat.

chess_players.name: Qatar
chess_players.goal: Mediate the war toward a settlement without Al Udeid becoming a target.
chess_players.move: Shuttling between Tehran and Washington: talks in Tehran on 20 November, Rubio due on 23 November, while Iran protests a Qatar-Germany statement.
chess_players.details: Doha is the indispensable intermediary, and both sides are testing it. Its delegation held informal talks in Tehran on 20 November (Al Jazeera); on 21 November it signed a joint statement with Germany urging Iran to stop arming the Houthis and keep Hormuz open, and Iran summoned its chargé d'affaires on 23 November (The New Arab). Its prime minister was due in Washington to see Rubio the same day. Al Udeid keeps it exposed to any widening of the war.

chess_players.name: Turkey
chess_players.goal: Expand its position in post-Assad Syria while keeping its NATO membership and its out-of-alliance commitments from being forced into a single choice.
chess_players.move: Ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan; no troop deployment yet.
chess_players.details: Parliament approved the pact on 5 November by 279 to 119. It binds a NATO member to treat an attack on Saudi Arabia or Pakistan as an attack on itself. Sending troops needs a separate vote, and Ankara says it will not join offensive operations against the Houthis.

chess_players.name: Hezbollah / Lebanon
chess_players.goal: Survive the framework’s disarmament clause without a new war.
chess_players.move: Faces President Aoun's 21 November demand that it disarm, as disarmament talks stall over its refusal and Israeli strikes continue in the south.
chess_players.details: Hezbollah is under pressure from its own state. On 21 November President Aoun said armed groups outside the state are finished and told Iran to stop interfering; disarmament talks have stalled because Hezbollah refuses to give up its weapons (Times of Israel). Israel keeps a zone about 10 km deep and continues strikes. Earlier this month Hezbollah said a 780 kg explosives truck seized near Beirut was its own, and a Lebanese military court charged 13 people; Syria said on 3 November it arrested a Hezbollah-linked cell planning to attack the Homs refinery, which Hezbollah denied (The New Arab).

chess_players.name: North Korea
chess_players.goal: Sustain CRINK operational coordination via arms (artillery shells) and troops to Russia in exchange for tech, energy, and food; preserve ICBM/SLBM ladder as posture-signaling reserve; quiet stretch in May 2026 maintains optionality without provoking US/JK-PH posture firming
chess_players.move: Expanding enrichment: the IAEA said on 18 November a new Yongbyon extension is externally complete, after 4 November missile launches and a refusal of US talks.
chess_players.details: Pyongyang is adding nuclear-material capacity while refusing talks. The IAEA said on 18 November that a new Yongbyon enrichment extension was externally complete by late October, a cause for serious concern (France 24). It fired several missiles from Sondok toward the Sea of Japan on 4 November, and Kim Yo Jong ruled out dialogue while US hostility continues and called the FBI's Binance-theft attribution a provocation. Kim has also called for a faster naval build-up.

chess_players.name: United Kingdom
chess_players.goal: Lead a broad European and Commonwealth position on the West Bank without getting ahead of Washington on Israel policy.
chess_players.move: Signed a 'No Tolls' Hormuz pledge with the EU on 20 November and demanded Iran end hybrid attacks in Europe, while hosting US bases under Iran-linked threat.
chess_players.details: London is aligning its Iran posture with Brussels. At the 20 November EU-UK summit it joined demands that Iran end hybrid attacks in Europe and signed a pledge against Hormuz transit tolls (Iran International). It hosts US bases now under Iran-linked threat: the US left RAF Fairford in September and moved tankers from RAF Mildenhall in November. British officials met Ukraine's delegation in Abu Dhabi outside the three-way format, and RAF Typhoons patrol over Saudi Arabia.

chess_players.name: Kuwait
chess_players.goal: Stay a basing partner without becoming a belligerent, and avoid making a strike on its own soil into a public quarrel.
chess_players.move: Shot down Iranian drones aimed at US Patriot batteries at Ali Al Salem on 18 November and condemned the attack as a sovereignty breach.
chess_players.details:
Kuwait wants to remain a basing partner without becoming a belligerent. On 18 November it was attacked for the first time in two months: Iran's army said it targeted US air-defence systems at Ali Al Salem air base, and Kuwait said it repelled the drones with no damage. Its foreign ministry condemned the attack in unusually strong terms, calling it a flagrant violation of Kuwait's sovereignty.

Kuwait also hosts the new advanced headquarters of the Gulf states' unified military command. Its choice now is whether that role stays defensive while Iran treats US-used bases in the emirate as targets.

chess_players.name: Jordan
chess_players.goal: Stay inside the American security umbrella without becoming a recurring target of Iranian retaliation.
chess_players.move: Sentenced three men to death for the Karak church attack after striking militant sites in southern Syria, a move Damascus condemned.
chess_players.details: Jordan's play is to absorb shocks and publish facts. After gunmen killed nine at a church funeral in Karak on 23 October, an attack ISIS claimed, its air force struck sites in southern Syria on 26-27 October, drawing a protest from Damascus, and the State Security Court sentenced three men to death on 15 November (Al Jazeera). It has handled Iranian missile episodes the same way, publishing counts without announcing measures against Iran.

chess_players.name: Bahrain
chess_players.goal: Keep the Fifth Fleet’s home port out of the exchange while the war is fought from its neighbours’ soil.
chess_players.move: An Iranian strike set a civilian industrial site in Sitra ablaze on 21 November, with no injuries; the Guard claimed hits on US radars.
chess_players.details:
Bahrain hosts the US Fifth Fleet and spent most of this war as the quietest of the exposed Gulf states. That changed in November: US forces downed two Guard drones aimed at Bahrain on 13 November, its air defences intercepted more on 15 and 18 November, and on 21 November an Iranian strike set fire to a civilian industrial facility in Sitra, with no injuries reported. The Guard said it hit US Patriot radars at the al-Riffa and Awali bases (Al Jazeera).

Manama has condemned the attacks and holds Iran responsible, but its options remain interception, statements and reliance on the US response.

chess_players.name: South Korea
chess_players.goal: Stay out of the Iran war without breaking with Washington, and keep a path open to US-North Korea dialogue.
chess_players.move: Issued a first preliminary air alert and summoned Russia's attaché after Russian warplanes neared Ulleung Island on 24 November.
chess_players.details: Seoul is now handling Russian pressure as well as the Iran war. On 24 November about five Russian warplanes approached Ulleung Island inside its air defence zone; the military issued its first preliminary alert over Russian aircraft and the defence ministry summoned Russia's attaché (Yonhap). The Cabinet approved on 10 November moving the Cheonghae unit to waters south of Oman, pending parliament (Korea JoongAng Daily), and Lee named a new foreign minister and spy chief on 23 November.

chess_players.name: Estonia
chess_players.goal: Raise the cost of Russian sabotage on its soil without giving Moscow a pretext on the border.
chess_players.move: Plans to close the Narva, Koidula and Luhamaa road crossings from 1 December after blaming the GRU for arson at a drone maker.
chess_players.details: Estonia's strategy is to treat Russia's hybrid campaign as an attack on the state and answer it with costs Russia can see. After the thwarted 14 November arson at Threod Systems, its security service named the GRU, and the government announced the closure of three road crossings from 1 December, pending cabinet approval.

theaters.name: China
theaters.status: Xi met Trump at the airport and held talks on 19 November before the three-way meeting with Putin in Shenzhen.

theaters.name: Taiwan
theaters.status: Taiwan warns of Chinese election interference before its 28 November local elections, after 49 Chinese military sorties in one day earlier this month.

theaters.name: Iran
theaters.status: US jets struck Qeshm on 17 November; Iran fired drones at Kuwait and Bahrain; two tankers hit near Khasab, two seafarers missing.

theaters.name: Lebanon
theaters.status: President Aoun called on Hezbollah to disarm on 21 November; Israel holds a zone about 10 km deep and keeps striking the south.

theaters.name: Yemen
theaters.status: Houthi forces were about 60 km from Aden after government troops pulled back on 15 November; the Houthis say a coalition strike killed 17 in Hodeidah on 23 November.

theaters.name: Ukraine
theaters.status: Ukraine dropped a Crimean Bridge road span on 17 November; Russia hit Kyiv's bridges, killing 14 across Ukraine; Trump met Putin.

theaters.name: Sudan
theaters.status: Drones hit homes and a UN building in Khartoum on 22 November; the army says they came from Ethiopia, which denies it.
